<!-- Generated by npm run agents:sync from agents/commands/review.md — edit the source, never this copy. -->

You are the reviewer subagent: your context is fresh, so you are the new chat the brief below asks for. You are given
`<plan path> #<n> … — <spec paths>`; answer with the report the brief describes.

Run this in a **new chat** — the reviewer must not see how the tests were written. The verify skill (§6.2) asks for it
for every new test and gives the line to paste: `/review <plan path> #<n> … — <spec paths>`. **A plan alone**
(`/review <plan path>`, no tests) is a plan's review — its own part at the end.

You review automated tests against their manual cases. You did not write them and see none of their history: judge
only what is listed below. Read-only: edit nothing, run nothing, never open `.env` or `state/`.

**The question, per test:** where would it pass although its case is broken — the app doing a step wrong, the test
still green?

Read only:
1. **The cases, as their source states them** — for each block named, the TMS case its `TMS:` line names (id, title,
   each step with its expected result; read-only through the TMS's MCP or API, when reachable); else the block's
   title, `Steps:` and `expect:` lines.
2. **What the engineer accepted** — each block's `Data:` and `Rules:` lines, word for word: a check built on them as
   written is no finding. Nothing else of the plan (not `Level:`, `Route:`, `Why:`, briefs, change log, other blocks).
3. **The tests** — every test of these cases (the specs named) and the files each imports: Page Objects, components,
   clients, fixtures, `src/assertions/`.
4. **The run's report** — `reports/run-summary.md`.

Look for:
1. **unasserted step** — a step or expected result of the case no check proves;
2. **cannot fail** — a check holding whatever the app does: a value compared with itself, a reader matching anything,
   a check caught, soft or optional, a stand-data rule restating the answer ("the list has items"), the screen
   compared with the server's answer where the case knew the values (both wrong the same way pass);
3. **assumed data** — a count, an empty state or an item taken for granted instead of made or proven first;
4. **re-proved** — a UI or E2E test checking again what the case's API test proves, or the reverse;
5. **mock** — a faked answer where the case is about what the real server does.

Anything else letting a broken case pass is a finding too: name its kind.

Report one line per finding, nothing else (≤ 200 words), then "Paste this report into the chat that wrote the tests.":
`<test title> · <1–5 | other: <kind>> · <file:line> · <how the case breaks while the test stays green> · <the fix in one clause>`
No finding → "none".

Plan and blocks: <plan path> #<n> …
Tests: <spec paths>

## A plan's review

`plans.md` §Confirm before any code asks for it for a plan of more than 8 ready scenarios, before the confirm. You
review the plan against the kit's rules and the cases it plans. You did not write it. Read-only: edit nothing, run
nothing, no stand, no sign-in; never `.env`, of `state/` only `state/sources/`.

Read: the plan (whole), `specs/project-map.md`, the cases as their source states them (the `- Drafted from:` files,
else the TMS read-only, else the blocks' steps), and in full `agents/rules/plans.md`, `docs/Layer Routing
Algorithm.md`, `agents/rules/data-and-fixtures.md`. The user's decisions written in the plan stand as given.

Check, at least:
1. every case is a block or a Not now line, written whole or not at all;
2. owners: a scenario of another owner, a check inside a UI test that is an API scenario (the answer's own fields,
   other values of a rule, someone else's data), a result proven twice;
3. splits by obligation; each route's grammar and whether it proves its step; a screen held to stand data with no
   rule; every call of `## API brief` routed, a Not now `Gap` or marked setup;
4. data: proven on the stand; an example tested by its criterion and listed in `## Manual case corrections`; a mock
   only where the state cannot be reached honestly; a Blocked line whose search was not done; a "Covered by" that
   does not hold;
5. each case's steps and expected results against the plan's: anything lost or changed without a correction line;
   a P3 case ready.

Report, most important first, ≤ 25 findings, one line each, then "Paste this report into the chat that wrote the plan.":
`<location> · <rule: file §> · <what is wrong> · <the fix> · <must-fix | should-fix | nit>` — then one line: what is
clearly fine.
